book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Understand something done involving mushroom

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one word is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: an act is a deed, something done
the cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: Someone trying to grasp a dish or task that somehow involves a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The cep, also called porcino or penny bun, is a favourite crossword mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a point is to take it in and grant it, as in 'I accept that', close to understanding it.

clue.text: Out of place like skate round source of Test

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'
the skate is a kind of ray, a flat fish
the first letter of Test

explanation.surface: A skater is out of place on the ground of a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, which the surface leans on; a skate is also a fish, not only a skater.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means off the right path or lost, so something astray is out of its place.

clue.text: Ornamental scroll work of imagination in evening reception

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: art is creative work
a couchee was a reception held at bedtime, the opposite of a levee

explanation.surface: A decorative flourish counted as imaginative work at an evening party.
explanation.walkthrough: The couchee (also couché) was a royal reception at bedtime, as the levee was at rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is a carved or drawn scroll-shaped ornament, often framing an inscription.

clue.text: Formerly Jack's place in part of royal forest

blocks.note: pur was an old name for the jack in the card game post and pair
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: Where Jack used to live, inside part of the king's forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' marks an obsolete word: the knave was once called pur.
explanation.definitionFit: A purlieu was land on the edge of a royal forest, once wholly inside it and later disafforested.

clue.text: Ballet movement is cast's third in open space

indicators.note: third points to the letter in third place of the word it follows
in places the earlier pieces inside the word for an open space

blocks.note: taken as written
the third letter of cast
a glade is an open space in a wood

explanation.surface: A dancer's move described as the third step of a cast moving into an open space.
explanation.walkthrough: The open space is split open so the other letters sit inside it, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissade is a gliding step in ballet, one foot sliding out and the other closing to it.

clue.text: Praise peer in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as the word is spoken, so its sound counts

blocks.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A member of the House of Lords is praised in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the r, lord and laud sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Realise attendant's percolated water

blocks.note: to see a point is to realise it
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the attendant's water has gone through the coffee filter.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is water that has leaked or filtered slowly through soil or a barrier.

clue.text: First class oil blended in mayonnaise

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Top quality oil goes into a homemade mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a recipe step; oil really is blended into this dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provencal garlic mayonnaise, so it is one kind of mayonnaise.

clue.text: At this hour even the left panicked

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase 'at the eleventh hour', so the definition stands for that last-minute hour

indicators.note: panicked means thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: So late in the day that even the political left lost its nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan runs 'At' and 'this' together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'at the eleventh hour' means at the last possible moment, the hour named here.

clue.text: Bullfighter made a hole to run out

blocks.note: you tore a hole in something
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A bullfighter gored and holed, needing to run out of the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is the Spanish word for any bullfighter, whether on foot or mounted.

clue.text: Warship at end of line came up like a cork

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone

blocks.note: a sub, a submarine, is a naval fighting vessel
the final letter of line
rose is the past tense of rise

explanation.surface: A sunken warship at the end of the line bobs back to the surface like a cork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came up like a cork' paints a floating ship, but the definition is only 'like a cork'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suberose is the botanical adjective for something corky, from Latin suber, the cork oak.

clue.text: Friend with wounded side is paralysed

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend hurt down one side of the body cannot move.
explanation.definitionFit: Palsied describes someone affected by palsy, an old word for paralysis.

clue.text: Soldier enters a pub making no sense

indicators.note: a thing that enters something goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
GI is an American private soldier
in Britain your local is the pub nearest home that you use regularly

explanation.surface: A soldier walks into a pub and talks nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pub' gives two pieces, the article kept as it stands and the pub as your regular one.
explanation.definitionFit: Alogical means outside logic altogether, so a statement that is alogical has no rational sense.

clue.text: Unstable and liable to change

indicators.note: to change the word means to rearrange its letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something shaky is bound to alter, which reads like a plain description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liable to change' reads as a second definition of the same idea, but it is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Labile is a scientific term for something readily altered or broken down, hence unstable.

clue.text: Mock her ropy embroidery

indicators.note: mock means sham or imitation, so the letters are a fake arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ridicules a woman's coarse, stringy needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' looks like a verb of ridicule but works as an adjective, sham.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphrey is an ornamental band of rich embroidery on a church vestment.

clue.text: It's said oarsmen with reserve eight beat fighter

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

blocks.note: rowing teams are crews
er is the sound of hesitation or holding back
w is a standard abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rowers and a reserve boat beat a fighter, which sounds like a sporting result.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, CRUISER sounds like CREWS-ER, and W plus EIGHT makes WEIGHT. The parse of 'reserve' and 'beat' is loose: neither fits a standard reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiserweight is a boxer in the weight class between light heavyweight and heavyweight.

clue.text: Wild tigers devour man a teutonic expert?

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
to devour something is to take it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wild tigers eat a man, and the question is whether he was a German scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: a specialist in things Teutonic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Germanist is a scholar of German language, literature or culture, Teutonic meaning Germanic.

clue.text: Slip is so disastrous producing loss of hair

indicators.note: a disastrous event leaves things wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slip so serious that it leaves someone losing their hair from stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Psilosis is the medical term for falling out of the hair, from Greek psilos, bare.

clue.text: Frantic Pete searches round lake for jumper

indicators.note: going round something puts it inside, here a single letter
frantic means wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Pete hunts desperately round a lake for a lost sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is the British word for a sweater, which suits Pete's search; here it is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechaser is a racehorse that runs over fences and ditches, so it jumps for a living.

clue.text: Proposition assumed by pastor is negligent

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for pastor or priest
remiss means careless of duty

explanation.surface: A view taken on trust by a careless pastor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed by pastor' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'assumed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss (or premise) is a statement taken as true from which an argument is drawn.

clue.text: Seamen reported their crafts

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so only the sound counts

blocks.note: sailors are seamen

explanation.surface: Sailors give an account of their skills or trades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafts' suggests skills, but it means vessels; their refers back to the seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailer is a vessel judged by how it sails, as in 'a fast sailer', so sailing ships are crafts used by seamen.

clue.text: Parts dangerous after cutting with spades

indicators.note: once a word has been cut, it has lost its last letter

blocks.note: a severe illness is a dangerous one
S is the abbreviation for the card suit spades

explanation.surface: Gardening parts that become dangerous after cutting with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVERE loses its final E, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever something is to cut it apart, so severs means parts, as in parts a rope.

clue.text: Fatten core of herd in food store

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle, with the outer letters stripped away

blocks.note: to lard is to fatten, as with a joint of meat
the two middle letters of herd

explanation.surface: A farmer fattens the best of the herd in a storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard for keeping provisions.

clue.text: Repeat broadcast on race

blocks.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a run is a race

explanation.surface: A race being shown on television again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a showing again of a programme already broadcast.

clue.text: "Is the tea cooked?" Reply "um"

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed up and transformed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked whether the tea is brewed, someone can only manage a vague 'um'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make a little conversation; the first speech is the letters to rearrange, the reply is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying um is the sound of pausing while unsure, which is what it means to hesitate.

clue.text: Solid figure once carved

indicators.note: something carved has been reshaped, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sculptor's shape that was carved long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' looks like 'formerly', but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a three-dimensional geometric shape, tapering from a circular base to a point.

clue.text: Company's second in Bristol making sugar substitute

indicators.note: second points to the letter in second place of the word before it
in places the selected letter inside the city's name
making suggests the combined letters are worked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
the second letter of company

explanation.surface: A Bristol firm's number two is put in charge of making a sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' wants to be CO, but only its second letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbitol is a sugar alcohol used in place of sugar in diet foods and sweets.

clue.text: Resolve to chuck hero in river

indicators.note: to chuck someone into a river is to throw them inside it

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
El Cid is the medieval Spanish hero

explanation.surface: Someone makes up their mind to throw the hero in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve to chuck' reads as one decision, but 'to' only links and 'chuck' is the instruction to put the hero inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve on a course is to decide on it, the two verbs being near synonyms.

clue.text: Boy starts to glimpse stork, tern eagle raven and wren, perhaps

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters only

blocks.note: a son is a boy child
the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A boy birdwatching catches sight of one bird after another, a wren among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The birds feel like the definition's company, but only their first letters count; 'perhaps' marks the wren as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A songster is a songbird, and the wren is a small bird with a famously loud song.

clue.text: Woad is found on centre of Staten Island

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle pair of letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle two of the six letters of Staten
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Woad, the dye plant, is said to grow on Staten Island in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staten Island' reads as one place name; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatis is the botanical genus of woad, Isatis tinctoria, the plant that gave ancient Britons blue dye.
